metaDescription: Six rice cookers with steam trays compared by capacity, tray material and control type, from AROMA multicookers and Cosori to a Zojirushi 3 cup steamer.
expertTake: The Cosori 10 cup fuzzy logic cooker is the best rice cooker with a steamer for most households, combining fuzzy logic rice with saute and steam functions. The AROMA ARC-363 is the value pick for one to three people, and cooks who steam large quantities should look at the 20 cup AROMA. Steaming is a bonus, so rice quality should drive the decision. Choose by the rice you want, then add steam.
introParagraphs: A steam tray turns a rice cooker into a one-pot meal maker. Vegetables, fish or dumplings sit above the rice and cook in the steam that rice produces, so dinner arrives in one pass with one pot to wash. A steamer also keeps nutrients and textures that boiling can wash out. Meal preppers often steam a protein and a vegetable together while the rice cooks, which saves a pot and a burner.

Steaming on these machines is by eye or by a simple timer. What matters is how the tray fits, how much water the pot holds, and whether the control handles rice well while the steam does its work. Buyers often forget to check how the tray stores when not in use.

products.name: Cosori Rice Cooker 10 Cup Fuzzy Logic, 18-in-1, Ceramic Pot
products.description:
The Cosori is a 10 cup fuzzy logic cooker with eighteen functions, including steaming, sauteing and slow cooking. Different white and brown rice types and texture options are available, with a 24 hour keep warm and delay timer.

The steam function is one of many, and the fuzzy logic means the rice below cooks well while the tray steams above. Compared with the AROMA models, it adds fuzzy logic and a ceramic pot. Compared with the Zojirushi 3 cup, it is far larger and more versatile.

Use soft utensils on the ceramic coating and wash the lid and vent regularly. Owner feedback patterns favor it for being a true all-in-one that does not force compromises on the rice. The saute mode lets you brown aromatics first. It is also the one to buy if the same pot will cook oatmeal on weekday mornings. The ceramic pot makes cleanup after steaming simple, and the lid vent can be pulled apart for rinsing. Compared with the AROMA Digital it holds far more rice.
products.bestFor: Families that want rice, steaming and other functions in one pot.

products.name: AROMA ARC-363-1NGB 3 Cup Uncooked, 6 Cup Cooked Rice Cooker and Steamer
products.description:
The ARC-363 is a small multicooker with a 3 cup uncooked, 6 cup cooked capacity, one-touch operation and an included steam tray that lets you steam foods above while rice, soup or another meal cooks below. It follows a set it and forget it design.

It is the lowest tier pick and the simplest. It suits one to three people. One-touch means a single on/off cycle, so it handles white rice well but is less sure with brown rice.

Wipe the plate and wash the tray. Compared with the AROMA Digital, it has no steam preset but costs less. Owner feedback patterns favor its simplicity for dorm and office use. Owner feedback patterns note that the tray is the part people use most, so keep a spare if you steam daily. The footprint is small enough for a bedroom desk. It is cheap enough to be a second cooker in a vacation home.
products.bestFor: Singles and couples who want to steam vegetables with rice.

products.name: AROMA Digital Rice Cooker 4 Cup Uncooked, 8 Cup Cooked, Steamer
products.description:
The AROMA Digital offers programmable controls with white rice, brown rice, steam and flash rice presets, and automatic keep warm after each cycle. A steam tray lets you steam meat, vegetables and more while rice cooks below.

It has a dedicated steam setting, which sets it apart from the one-touch ARC-363. It lacks fuzzy logic, so the rice is good rather than refined.

Wash the tray and the lid after use. The brown rice preset helps where one-touch cookers fall short. Compared with the Cosori, it is smaller and lacks fuzzy logic. The digital panel lets you set steam time directly instead of watching the clock. That matters when you steam fish, which goes from done to dry in minutes. The steam preset runs a set time, so check the food at the end.
products.bestFor: A digital cooker with a steam preset on a budget.

products.name: AROMA Select Stainless 6 Cup Cooked / 1.2 Qt Pot-Style Cooker and Steamer
products.description:
This pot-style cooker has a coating-free 304 stainless steel pot and a stainless steam tray. It prepares up to 6 cups of cooked rice and lets you steam meat and vegetables while rice cooks below. One-touch operation keeps use simple.

The stainless pot appeals to buyers who want to avoid nonstick coatings. Rice sticks more on stainless, so wash soon after cooking.

It suits a family and meal prep. The pot is dishwasher safe. Compared with the Cosori, it has no fuzzy logic but avoids any ceramic coating. Owner feedback patterns favor stainless for anyone worried about coatings. A coating-free pot is dishwasher safe, so cleanup after fish and curries is easier than with a coated inner pan. The 1.2 qt volume suits one to three people.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want stainless and a steam tray.

products.name: Zojirushi 3 Cup Rice Cooker and Steamer, Glass Lid
products.description:
The Zojirushi 3 cup is a cooker and steamer with a single-switch control, a see-through glass lid with a stay-cool knob and stay-cool handles. A glass lid lets you watch the steaming progress.

The brand name signals build quality. It is simple and durable, and it holds food warm after cooking.

Wipe the plate and wash the lid. Compared with the AROMA ARC-363, it costs more but is built to last longer. The steaming tray is simple and sturdy. The glass lid lets you see the steam condensing without letting heat escape. Stay-cool handles help when you carry the cooker to the table.
products.bestFor: Small households that want a durable steamer.

products.name: AROMA Professional Plus ARC-5000SB 20 Cup Cooked Digital Cooker and Steamer
products.description:
The ARC-5000SB is a family-size digital cooker with a 20 cup cooked capacity yielding from 4 to 20 cups of cooked rice. It has a built-in steam function for cooking nutrient-rich meals above rice or soup, and also works as a slow cooker.

Its size makes it a good fit for large families and meal prep. It is also a multicooker for jambalaya or cakes.

It is large and needs shelf space. Clean the lid and vent. Compared with the Cosori, it is bigger and plainer. The stainless exterior wipes clean. It doubles as a slow cooker for stews, though the slow mode is gentle. The size also suits batch cooking rice for the week. Compared with the Cosori, it lacks fuzzy logic but has a larger pot.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Steam trays are plastic or stainless. Stainless, as on the AROMA Select, does not stain or warp. Check that the tray sits clear of the rice and leaves room for the lid. A tray with small holes keeps small vegetables from falling through. A common mistake is stacking food in a thick pile, which steams the outside and leaves the middle raw. Spread it in a single layer.

Steaming needs water, and the pot must hold enough for both rice and steam. The AROMA 3 cup is tight, while the 20 cup ARC-5000SB gives room. Do not exceed the max line. Steaming for a long time can boil the pot dry, so check the water. If you steam with rice, the rice water supplies the steam, so a pot filled to the minimum line may run dry.

Fuzzy logic on the Cosori adjusts heat while you steam above. One-touch cookers like the ARC-363 run a single cycle and may overcook the rice if the tray adds heat load. Keep the food on the tray in a single layer for even steaming. Brown rice needs longer than most steamed foods, so pair it with long-cooking vegetables such as carrots. Rice can overcook if the tray blocks the steam path.

Basic models steam by eye, with timing guided by the rice cycle. Digital models like the AROMA Digital offer a steam preset. Fish needs about ten minutes, dense vegetables longer. Steam fish and tender vegetables in the last ten to fifteen minutes. Dumplings and buns need a lined tray to prevent sticking.

Stainless pots such as the AROMA Select do not scratch but rice sticks more. Nonstick and ceramic pots clean easily but need soft utensils. Stainless pots also resist scratching from steam tray feet. Stainless pots need a quick soak after cooking to release stuck rice.

Wash the tray, lid and vent after steaming, since fish and vegetable odors cling. Keep the outside of the pot dry before inserting. A soak in warm soapy water clears odors quickly. Wash the tray and lid in hot soapy water to remove fish odor.

specDecoder.meaning: A perforated tray above the rice that holds food for steaming. Some models include a second tier. It also lets steam circulate.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check whether it is plastic or stainless. Check the tray height against the rice level.

specDecoder.meaning: The cooked rice yield, roughly double the uncooked. Check this against your usual batch.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 20 cup ARC-5000SB serves up to 20 cups cooked. Check the cooked and uncooked numbers.

specDecoder.meaning: Sensing control that adjusts heat during the cycle. It helps when you cook rice while steaming above.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Cosori has it here. Check the menu for a steam mode.

specDecoder.meaning: A single on/off cycle. It does not offer timing control.
specDecoder.watchFor: The ARC-363 and Select use it. Check what the lever does when the cycle ends.

specDecoder.meaning: A cooker with a removable stainless pot instead of a coated inner pan. The stainless pot holds heat evenly.
specDecoder.watchFor: The AROMA Select uses it. Check dishwasher safety.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at trays, pots and cleaning access. Removable parts matter for odor control. Odor control is a practical concern.

cards.label: Stainless
cards.text: Does not stain or warp. Best here: AROMA Select.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A tray with holes, enough water for both, and a lid that seals. Cut vegetables small for even steaming. Line the tray with parchment for dumplings.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Cosori and AROMA Select handle steaming best. The ARC-5000SB also has a larger tray for bigger portions.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You steam daily or feed a family. The Cosori or ARC-5000SB fits. The upper tier also buys fuzzy logic or a larger pot.

cards.text: You steam occasionally. The ARC-363 is enough. Use the savings on a bamboo steamer for occasional use.

maintenance.why: Fish and vegetable odors cling to trays. A soak in soapy water clears odors. Soak the tray in hot soapy water before scrubbing.
Starch builds up in the vent. A toothbrush clears the vent. Starch dries hard in the vent if left.
Debris causes uneven heating. Unplug and cool first. A dirty plate can cause scorching.
A wet pot hisses and contacts poorly. Wipe the outside of the pot. Moisture on the contacts can trip the cooker.
A flaking coating should be replaced. Do not use a pot with exposed metal. A scratched pot can flake into food.

faq.q: Can I steam while the rice cooks?
faq.a: Yes. Put the tray in and add food; steam rises from the rice water. Keep the lid closed to hold the steam. Check the water level occasionally for long steams.
